topics.name: Number
points: N1 Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥
N2 Apply the four operations, including formal written methods, to integers, decimals, simple fractions and mixed numbers; place value
N3 Relationships between operations, inverse operations; priority of operations including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals
N4 Prime numbers, factors, multiples, HCF, LCM, prime factorisation and the unique factorisation theorem
N5 Systematic listing strategies, including the product rule for counting
N6 Positive integer powers and real roots; recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, 5; estimate powers and roots
N7 Calculate with roots and integer indices; calculate with fractional indices
N8 Calculate exactly with fractions, multiples of π and surds; simplify surds and rationalise denominators
N9 Calculate with and interpret standard form A × 10ⁿ
N10 Terminating decimals and fractions; change recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa
N11 Identify and work with fractions in ratio problems
N12 Interpret fractions and percentages as operators
N13 Standard units of mass, length, time, money and other measures, including compound measures
N14 Estimate answers; check calculations using approximation and estimation
N15 Round to an appropriate degree of accuracy; error intervals due to truncation or rounding
N16 Apply and interpret limits of accuracy, including upper and lower bounds

topics.name: Algebra
points: A1 Use and interpret algebraic notation
A2 Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae
A3 Expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors
A4 Simplify and manipulate expressions: like terms, brackets, factorising, laws of indices, quadratics, surds and algebraic fractions
A5 Use standard formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject
A6 Equations and identities; argue mathematically to show expressions are equivalent, including proofs
A7 Functions with inputs and outputs; inverse and composite functions
A8 Work with coordinates in all four quadrants
A9 Straight-line graphs: y = mx + c, parallel and perpendicular lines, line through two points
A10 Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and algebraically
A11 Roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratics; turning points by completing the square
A12 Recognise, sketch and interpret linear, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal, exponential and trigonometric graphs
A14 Plot and interpret graphs in real contexts, including reciprocal and exponential graphs
A17 Solve linear equations in one unknown, including unknowns on both sides
A18 Solve quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square and the quadratic formula
A19 Solve simultaneous equations: linear/linear and linear/quadratic
A21 Translate situations into expressions or equations; derive, solve and interpret
A22 Solve linear and quadratic inequalities; represent solution sets on number lines, in set notation and graphs
A23 Generate terms of a sequence from term-to-term or position-to-term rules
A24 Recognise triangular, square, cube, Fibonacci-type, quadratic and geometric sequences
A25 Deduce expressions for the nth term of linear and quadratic sequences

topics.name: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
points: R1 Change between standard and compound units (speed, rates of pay, density, pressure)
R2 Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps
R3 Express one quantity as a fraction of another
R4 Use ratio notation, including reduction to simplest form
R5 Divide a quantity in a given ratio; apply ratio to real contexts and problems
R6 Express a multiplicative relationship between two quantities as a ratio or fraction
R7 Understand and use proportion as equality of ratios
R8 Relate ratios to fractions and to linear functions
R9 Percentages: percentage change, original value, simple interest and financial maths
R10 Direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations
R11 Use compound units such as speed, unit pricing, density and pressure
R12 Compare lengths, areas and volumes using ratio; links to similarity and trigonometric ratios
R13 Inverse proportion as proportion to 1/Y; construct and interpret proportion equations
R14 Gradient as rate of change; graphs of direct and inverse proportion
R16 Growth and decay problems, compound interest and iterative processes

topics.name: Geometry and measures
points: G1 Conventional geometric terms and notation; labelling triangles; drawing from descriptions
G2 Ruler and compass constructions and loci
G3 Angle facts: at a point, on a line, parallel lines, angles in triangles and polygons
G4 Properties of special quadrilaterals, triangles and other plane figures
G5 Congruence criteria for triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS)
G6 Use angle facts, congruence and similarity to derive results and simple proofs
G7 Transformations: rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement (fractional and negative scale factors)
G9 Circle definitions: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector, segment
G11 Solve geometrical problems on coordinate axes
G12 Properties of faces, edges and vertices of 3D shapes
G13 Construct and interpret plans and elevations of 3D shapes
G14 Standard units of measure and related concepts
G15 Measure line segments and angles, including maps, scale drawings and bearings
G16 Area of triangles, parallelograms and trapezia; volume of prisms and cylinders
G17 Circles, composite shapes; surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and frustums
G18 Arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors
G19 Similar figures: relationships between lengths, areas and volumes
G20 Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios in 2D and 3D
G21 Exact values of sin, cos and tan
G24 Describe translations as 2D vectors
G25 Vector arithmetic and geometric proofs using vectors

topics.name: Probability
points: P1 Record, describe and analyse outcomes of probability experiments using tables and frequency trees
P2 Randomness, fairness and equally likely events; expected outcomes
P3 Relative expected frequency and theoretical probability; the 0 to 1 scale
P4 Probabilities of exhaustive sets of outcomes and of mutually exclusive events sum to 1
P5 Empirical unbiased samples tend towards theoretical distributions as sample size increases
P6 Enumerate sets systematically using tables, grids, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams
P7 Possibility spaces for single and combined experiments; theoretical probabilities
P8 Probability of independent and dependent combined events, including tree diagrams
P9 Conditional probability using two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams

topics.name: Statistics
points: S1 Infer properties of populations from a sample; limitations of sampling
S2 Tables, charts and diagrams, including time series line graphs
S3 Histograms with equal and unequal class widths; cumulative frequency graphs
S4 Compare distributions: averages, range, box plots, quartiles and inter-quartile range
S5 Apply statistics to describe a population
S6 Scatter graphs, correlation, lines of best fit, interpolation and extrapolation
